citations.title: Three Sisters garden (corn, bean, squash polyculture)
citations.org: Old Farmer’s Almanac / traditional Indigenous companion planting

templates.name: Three Sisters
templates.rationale: Classic polyculture: corn as a trellis, beans fix nitrogen, squash shades soil and deters pests.

templates.name: Tomato & basil guild
templates.rationale: Basil is a classic tomato companion—shared full-sun bed with aromatic underplanting between tomato stations.
templates.succession: Tuck quick lettuce or radish between young tomatoes until canopy fills (text note only).

templates.name: Nightshade & herbs
templates.rationale: Group heat-loving nightshades with basil/onion companions; keep full-sun crops together.

templates.name: Salad cut-and-come-again
templates.rationale: Dense leafy blocks at each crop’s own spacing for repeated harvest; mix radish for quick returns.
templates.succession: Sow radish every 10–14 days between slower lettuce/chard for succession harvests.

templates.name: Root bed
templates.rationale: Root crops in dedicated rows at catalog spacing; onions/garlic deter some pests among carrots and beets.
templates.succession: Interseed radish between carrot rows—radish matures and clears before carrots need the space.

templates.name: Brassica bed with companions
templates.rationale: Give brassicas wide spacing; edge with beet/onion companions. Avoid planting tomatoes beside cabbage.

templates.name: Cucumber & legumes
templates.rationale: Cucumbers with pea/bean nitrogen partners and radish as a traditional cucumber companion.

templates.name: Potato patch
templates.rationale: Potatoes in their own block with compatible bean/corn; keep clear of tomato, cucumber, and squash antagonists.
